mwalimu/cb03a75e.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/cb03a75e.text: You're Amani. Good. I'm Chief Inspector Wairimu. Everyone here calls me Mwalimu, and you'll find out why.
mwalimu/cb03a75e.error: no voice for mwalimu (mwalimu): run  cast  and  design --cast, or  design  then  pick mwalimu N

mwalimu/069a30a0.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/069a30a0.text: A driver at Ngara stage. Read the OB, go to the scene, look at everything twice. I'll be on the phone if you need me.
mwalimu/069a30a0.error: no voice for mwalimu (mwalimu): run  cast  and  design --cast, or  design  then  pick mwalimu N

mwalimu/1159ef7b.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/1159ef7b.error: no voice for mwalimu (mwalimu): run  cast  and  design --cast, or  design  then  pick mwalimu N

mwalimu/4b12b722.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/4b12b722.text: Registers are kept by people who weren't thinking about murder. That's why they're honest. Read every row, not just the one you came for.
mwalimu/4b12b722.error: no voice for mwalimu (mwalimu): run  cast  and  design --cast, or  design  then  pick mwalimu N

mwalimu/a0ba30c8.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/a0ba30c8.text: Times matter now. Your notebook has a Time tab: everyone you can place, lined up on one clock.
mwalimu/a0ba30c8.error: no voice for mwalimu (mwalimu): run  cast  and  design --cast, or  design  then  pick mwalimu N

mwalimu/f43dab2f.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/f43dab2f.text: Two places today. Both are in the folder. Go back and forth as often as you like. Walking costs you nothing.
mwalimu/f43dab2f.error: no voice for mwalimu (mwalimu): run  cast  and  design --cast, or  design  then  pick mwalimu N

mwalimu/bddc454b.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/bddc454b.text: When two papers talk about the same thing, put them side by side. Pin a line from each in your notebook and read the Pinned tab.
mwalimu/bddc454b.error: no voice for mwalimu (mwalimu): run  cast  and  design --cast, or  design  then  pick mwalimu N

mwalimu/34c26fc6.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/34c26fc6.text: A building, not a street. Before you decide who was where, ask how anyone got from one floor to another.
mwalimu/34c26fc6.error: no voice for mwalimu (mwalimu): run  cast  and  design --cast, or  design  then  pick mwalimu N

mwalimu/9e8c79ab.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/9e8c79ab.text: Open the Time tab. Every bar is someone you can place. The empty stretches deserve as much attention as the bars.
mwalimu/9e8c79ab.error: no voice for mwalimu (mwalimu): run  cast  and  design --cast, or  design  then  pick mwalimu N

mwalimu/ab8b26c2.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/ab8b26c2.text: Small writing matters. Tap any photograph to open it full size, then pinch or double-tap to look closer.
mwalimu/ab8b26c2.error: no voice for mwalimu (mwalimu): run  cast  and  design --cast, or  design  then  pick mwalimu N

mwalimu/0d52205a.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/0d52205a.text: Not everything that looks guilty is. When something points at a person, ask what else could explain it before you write a name.
mwalimu/0d52205a.error: no voice for mwalimu (mwalimu): run  cast  and  design --cast, or  design  then  pick mwalimu N

mwalimu/b6baaa41.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/b6baaa41.text: A timetable says where a train should be. People tell you where they were. Hold one against the other.
mwalimu/b6baaa41.error: no voice for mwalimu (mwalimu): run  cast  and  design --cast, or  design  then  pick mwalimu N

mwalimu/5ae588ed.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/5ae588ed.text: Read every exhibit twice: once for what it shows, and once for what it ought to show.
mwalimu/5ae588ed.error: no voice for mwalimu (mwalimu): run  cast  and  design --cast, or  design  then  pick mwalimu N

mwalimu/7f2ed231.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/7f2ed231.text: This one takes three steps, not two. If your name rests on a single fact, you're not finished.
mwalimu/7f2ed231.error: no voice for mwalimu (mwalimu): run  cast  and  design --cast, or  design  then  pick mwalimu N

mwalimu/53256677.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/53256677.text: You can pin six facts. Keep the ones that belong together on the Pinned tab, and the board will show them too.
mwalimu/53256677.error: no voice for mwalimu (mwalimu): run  cast  and  design --cast, or  design  then  pick mwalimu N

mwalimu/45769964.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/45769964.text: Photographs have backgrounds. Open it full size and look past the people in front.
mwalimu/45769964.error: no voice for mwalimu (mwalimu): run  cast  and  design --cast, or  design  then  pick mwalimu N

mwalimu/60131cc2.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/60131cc2.text: Two blanks this time, judged together. Halima accepts both or neither, so be sure of each.
mwalimu/60131cc2.error: no voice for mwalimu (mwalimu): run  cast  and  design --cast, or  design  then  pick mwalimu N

mwalimu/ec170671.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/ec170671.text: Everything you find lands here by itself. People, places, exhibits, and times. You don't write, you think.
mwalimu/ec170671.error: no voice for mwalimu (mwalimu): run  cast  and  design --cast, or  design  then  pick mwalimu N

mwalimu/b208531b.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/b208531b.text: The board is yours. Drag things where they make sense to you, tie string between them. Nobody grades it.
mwalimu/b208531b.error: no voice for mwalimu (mwalimu): run  cast  and  design --cast, or  design  then  pick mwalimu N

mwalimu/72c0d5d5.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/72c0d5d5.text: Call me when you're stuck. Where to look, what to notice, or the answer. Each one costs you a star you haven't earned yet, never the case.
mwalimu/72c0d5d5.error: no voice for mwalimu (mwalimu): run  cast  and  design --cast, or  design  then  pick mwalimu N

mwalimu/ec32222d.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/ec32222d.text: The charge sheet. Only names you've actually found are in the bank. Halima reads every one.
mwalimu/ec32222d.error: no voice for mwalimu (mwalimu): run  cast  and  design --cast, or  design  then  pick mwalimu N

mwalimu/daf43b7a.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/daf43b7a.text: Detective. You can call me. "Where to look" names the thing that matters. "What to notice" shows you two facts that belong together. "The answer" fills a blank, and costs you more.
mwalimu/daf43b7a.error: no voice for mwalimu (mwalimu): run  cast  and  design --cast, or  design  then  pick mwalimu N

c001-p_kassim/7bd682f5.speaker: c001-p_kassim
c001-p_kassim/7bd682f5.text: Nine years he parked in that bay. Nine years.

c001-p_kassim/6238367b.speaker: c001-p_kassim
c001-p_kassim/6238367b.text: Moses was the chama treasurer for the 9N drivers. Strict with the book. He'd chase you for fifty bob.

c001-p_kassim/cb375881.speaker: c001-p_kassim
c001-p_kassim/cb375881.text: 9N is the route. K is the driver's initial. Every driver paints his tools, otherwise they walk to Githurai by morning.

c001-p_kassim/064b473b.speaker: c001-p_kassim
c001-p_kassim/064b473b.text: The boy shouts at everyone. He's at Kencom tonight on 551Q. Talk to Wanjiru on the radio if you want.

c001-p_kassim/7bfcfa31.speaker: c001-p_kassim
c001-p_kassim/7bfcfa31.text: Kamau? He drives KCZ 902M. Left on his 22:30 trip. He'll be back around quarter past eleven.

c001-p_mercy/29d8e092.speaker: c001-p_mercy
c001-p_mercy/29d8e092.text: I keep thinking I'll see him walking over for his smokie.

c001-p_mercy/89dd0751.speaker: c001-p_mercy
c001-p_mercy/89dd0751.text: Every night at ten, one smokie pasua, extra kachumbari. Tonight too. He was laughing.

c001-p_mercy/30e1dfc9.speaker: c001-p_mercy
c001-p_mercy/30e1dfc9.text: Mzee Kassim was right here with a smokie in his hand when we heard it. He dropped it.

c001-p_mercy/bf6fc4fc.speaker: c001-p_mercy
c001-p_mercy/bf6fc4fc.text: Kamau never buys from me. He says my smokies are small. I don't know him better than that.

c001-p_peter/84520016.speaker: c001-p_peter
c001-p_peter/84520016.text: Moses? Wueh. I heard on the radio.

c001-p_peter/64b9266e.speaker: c001-p_peter
c001-p_peter/64b9266e.text: He kept the chama book. We all owe the book something. I didn't touch him.

c001-p_peter/b44956df.speaker: c001-p_peter
c001-p_peter/b44956df.text: Chama, chama. Yes, I'm three contributions behind. So are half the drivers on 9N.

c001-p_peter/a9878344.speaker: c001-p_peter
c001-p_peter/a9878344.text: Every driver has a spanner. Mine went missing this week. Someone borrowed it.

c001-p_peter/cfbe03d2.speaker: c001-p_peter
c001-p_peter/cfbe03d2.text: Look all you want. I told you, it went missing.

c001-p_peter/4cebdebd.speaker: c001-p_peter
c001-p_peter/4cebdebd.text: I left on my 22:30 trip like every Friday.

c001-p_brian/9fecf362.speaker: c001-p_brian
c001-p_brian/9fecf362.text: I didn't even know until Mama Wanjiru told me.

c001-p_brian/7dd078c5.speaker: c001-p_brian
c001-p_brian/7dd078c5.text: He cut my daily pay by two hundred. I shouted. That's all. You don't kill a man for two hundred bob.

c001-p_brian/fb6cf193.speaker: c001-p_brian
c001-p_brian/fb6cf193.text: Kamau owes the chama. Everyone on 9N knows. Moses was going to the sacco chairman about it, that's what they were saying.

c001-p_brian/54f22525.speaker: c001-p_brian
c001-p_brian/54f22525.text: I was at Kencom all night filling 551Q.

c001-p_wanjiru/28e96899.speaker: c001-p_wanjiru
c001-p_wanjiru/28e96899.text: Otieno? He's been in my queue since ten to ten shouting 'Ngara, Ngara!' I'd have heard if he stopped.

c002-p_nancy/36db41e7.speaker: c002-p_nancy
c002-p_nancy/36db41e7.text: Eleven years he greeted me every morning. Every morning.

c002-p_nancy/c7f08d1a.speaker: c002-p_nancy
c002-p_nancy/c7f08d1a.text: Francis did his rounds every hour with that big torch. Every floor. He was proud of that torch.

c002-p_nancy/bccc5000.speaker: c002-p_nancy
c002-p_nancy/bccc5000.text: I clean Bidii Freight first, every morning. The bin is always just paper. Today there were shoes in it. Shoes!

c002-p_nancy/a39f537a.speaker: c002-p_nancy
c002-p_nancy/a39f537a.text: Collins and Francis shouted at each other last week about weekend shifts. Young men shout.

c002-p_nancy/4b4f4166.speaker: c002-p_nancy
c002-p_nancy/4b4f4166.text: Mzee Ali next door sits at his window all night. Nothing happens on this street he doesn't see.

c002-p_ali/ab178154.speaker: c002-p_ali
c002-p_ali/ab178154.text: I keep a book too. Askari to askari, we watch each other's doors.

c002-p_ali/5eddde50.speaker: c002-p_ali
c002-p_ali/5eddde50.text: A woman with a laptop bag, about twenty to nine. Francis let her in and wrote in his book. I didn't see her come out of the front.

c002-p_ali/3c073f9b.speaker: c002-p_ali
c002-p_ali/3c073f9b.text: The painter? He left before dark, at five or so. Singing.

c002-p_isaac/f2708638.speaker: c002-p_isaac
c002-p_isaac/f2708638.text: I told everyone. Don't walk on my corridor.

c002-p_isaac/6a67176b.speaker: c002-p_isaac
c002-p_isaac/6a67176b.text: Final coat at ten to five. That paint stays tacky till nine, ten at night. I told the whole floor.

c002-p_isaac/673669b1.speaker: c002-p_isaac
c002-p_isaac/673669b1.text: That's not my boot. My boots are size 44. And I walk on the cloth edges, like a professional.

c002-p_isaac/3110cb23.speaker: c002-p_isaac
c002-p_isaac/3110cb23.text: Call Pastor Kioko. Tuesday is choir. I've never missed a Tuesday.

c002-p_isaac/4ee2e569.speaker: c002-p_isaac
c002-p_isaac/4ee2e569.text: I signed out at ten past five and went to choir.

c002-p_collins/6ab9049a.speaker: c002-p_collins
c002-p_collins/6ab9049a.text: We argued about Saturdays. He wanted me to cover. I said no. It was nothing. Call my wife.

c002-p_collins/039b2ca8.speaker: c002-p_collins
c002-p_collins/039b2ca8.text: I was home in Kayole. I didn't like Francis, but I didn't come back here.

c002-p_rehema/bec36e37.speaker: c002-p_rehema
c002-p_rehema/bec36e37.text: Kilele House? I was there last night, yes. Briefly.

c002-p_rehema/b8905cd3.speaker: c002-p_rehema
c002-p_rehema/b8905cd3.text: I keep a pair of office shoes in the office and go home in flats. Doesn't everyone?

c002-p_rehema/0f02da73.speaker: c002-p_rehema
c002-p_rehema/0f02da73.text: The audit is routine. Every year. I don't see what that has to do with Francis.

c002-p_rehema/ce90e102.speaker: c002-p_rehema
c002-p_rehema/ce90e102.text: I came back for some files and left. I didn't see anyone.

c003-p_mwikali/a71bed14.speaker: c003-p_mwikali
c003-p_mwikali/a71bed14.text: Drink. You'll need it. That girl was good to me.

c003-p_mwikali/292c38f1.speaker: c003-p_mwikali
c003-p_mwikali/292c38f1.text: Musyoka bought a ticket at twenty past five. Him! He hasn't travelled anywhere in ten years. Since February he touts for Kitui Star, two bays down.

c003-p_mwikali/aba46f8b.speaker: c003-p_mwikali
c003-p_mwikali/aba46f8b.text: Kevin has been under the Garissa bus with Gideon since five. I took them tea.

c003-p_mwikali/38c66daf.speaker: c003-p_mwikali
c003-p_mwikali/38c66daf.text: Lilian left at five past five like every Friday. She takes the Kayole matatu.

c003-p_gideon/7453ccf9.speaker: c003-p_gideon
c003-p_gideon/7453ccf9.text: He held the torch for me the whole check. Five to ten to six. Brake lines, belts, tyres. He didn't move.

c003-p_stephen/8c1ebeef.speaker: c003-p_stephen
c003-p_stephen/8c1ebeef.text: That woman lost me my job for two tickets. Two! Every manamba sells a few. But I didn't touch her.

c003-p_stephen/661782a0.speaker: c003-p_stephen
c003-p_stephen/661782a0.text: Anyone can open a luggage bay. Ask who drives that bus.

c003-p_stephen/76ee040b.speaker: c003-p_stephen
c003-p_stephen/76ee040b.text: I bought a ticket and changed my mind. Is that a crime?

c003-p_stephen/7e80f7a7.speaker: c003-p_stephen
c003-p_stephen/7e80f7a7.text: I never touched her. I never touched that box.

c003-p_kevin/492f39e4.speaker: c003-p_kevin
c003-p_kevin/492f39e4.text: She reported me twice this month. Now people will say I did it.

c003-p_kevin/752fbe92.speaker: c003-p_kevin
c003-p_kevin/752fbe92.text: She was strict about time. She was right, mostly. I'm late because the bus is old.

c003-p_kevin/40b05fa3.speaker: c003-p_kevin
c003-p_kevin/40b05fa3.text: I was under my bus. Ask Gideon.

c003-p_lilian/0922ea3a.speaker: c003-p_lilian
c003-p_lilian/0922ea3a.text: Ruth? But I left her at five. She was fine.

c003-p_lilian/be72dcf1.speaker: c003-p_lilian
c003-p_lilian/be72dcf1.text: We fought about rotas. Not about anything real. I'm sorry I said bad things about her.

c003-p_lilian/e21e1a78.speaker: c003-p_lilian
c003-p_lilian/e21e1a78.text: I handed over at five and went home. We didn't like each other. That's all.

c004-p_amos/6f6e746e.speaker: c004-p_amos
c004-p_amos/6f6e746e.text: She was saving for her diploma. Every shilling.

c004-p_amos/57c67af4.speaker: c004-p_amos
c004-p_amos/57c67af4.text: Njeru in 12? Pays cash every morning. Says he recruits for jobs in Qatar. He asked Faith which school she went to.

c004-p_amos/a6cd420d.speaker: c004-p_amos
c004-p_amos/a6cd420d.text: Room 7 shouted about hot water all evening. Then he got stuck in my lift. He'll want a refund.

c004-p_amos/f7e0f177.speaker: c004-p_amos
c004-p_amos/f7e0f177.text: Zawadi is the cook. She stays late Thursdays. She borrowed from Faith; everyone borrows from everyone here.

c004-p_zawadi/75f4f4b9.speaker: c004-p_zawadi
c004-p_zawadi/75f4f4b9.text: I went for candles. I went for candles and when I came back…

c004-p_zawadi/f3043212.speaker: c004-p_zawadi
c004-p_zawadi/f3043212.text: She said, 'Zawadi, run across, get candles, ours is the last one.' She laughed about it. That was eleven, ten past eleven.

c004-p_zawadi/9290c791.speaker: c004-p_zawadi
c004-p_zawadi/9290c791.text: Ask Hassan. The whole street was at his kiosk for candles and he had no coins for change.

c004-p_paul/dad8a340.speaker: c004-p_paul
c004-p_paul/dad8a340.text: Somebody left a candle by my door? People are careless in the dark.

c004-p_paul/e39f57d1.speaker: c004-p_paul
c004-p_paul/e39f57d1.text: Peter Ndungu? I don't know any Peter Ndungu. Njeru, Paul. You have my ID.

c004-p_paul/e995fa9a.speaker: c004-p_paul
c004-p_paul/e995fa9a.text: I was asleep in my room. I sleep early. I didn't even know there was a blackout.

c004-p_paul/0fc45db1.speaker: c004-p_paul
c004-p_paul/0fc45db1.text: I've never met that girl before this week.

c004-p_kennedy/a18ec0d9.speaker: c004-p_kennedy
c004-p_kennedy/a18ec0d9.text: Fifty minutes. Fifty minutes in that coffin.

c004-p_kennedy/f96958ed.speaker: c004-p_kennedy
c004-p_kennedy/f96958ed.text: Yes, I shouted at her about the water. I'm not proud of it. She said sorry like it was her fault.

c004-p_kennedy/5d7c75b0.speaker: c004-p_kennedy
c004-p_kennedy/5d7c75b0.text: I spent fifty minutes in a box between floors. Ask the technician.

c004-p_selina/5c1d43dc.speaker: c004-p_selina
c004-p_selina/5c1d43dc.text: I came in the front door at twenty to midnight. The desk was dark. I thought the girl had gone upstairs.

c004-p_selina/10203cbd.speaker: c004-p_selina
c004-p_selina/10203cbd.text: He was in that lift the whole time, believe me. He told me about it, loudly.

c005-p_bakari/e3f14cf3.speaker: c005-p_bakari
c005-p_bakari/e3f14cf3.text: Fifteen years he sold me the Taifa every morning. Fifteen years.

c005-p_bakari/29ff34a2.speaker: c005-p_bakari
c005-p_bakari/29ff34a2.text: He owed some people money. Everyone does. He was a good man with bad luck.

c005-p_bakari/e6c871d1.speaker: c005-p_bakari
c005-p_bakari/e6c871d1.text: Tony goes for the Taifa Jioni every afternoon. Industrial Area. He wasn't even here.

c005-p_esther/c774380e.speaker: c005-p_esther
c005-p_esther/c774380e.text: I saw him at twenty-five to three. He gave me my airtime and a joke.

c005-p_esther/2be05d7d.speaker: c005-p_esther
c005-p_esther/2be05d7d.text: Langat? The lender in the grey coat? Yes, that was him waiting at the kiosk, twenty-five to three. I know that coat; he collects at my church too.

c005-p_esther/7fc98c1b.speaker: c005-p_esther
c005-p_esther/7fc98c1b.text: A black umbrella, closed, hooked over his arm. It wasn't raining yet.

c005-p_bernard/e36cb541.speaker: c005-p_bernard
c005-p_bernard/e36cb541.text: I give those umbrellas to customers. Advertising. I lost one somewhere this week.

c005-p_bernard/145648e1.speaker: c005-p_bernard
c005-p_bernard/145648e1.text: Two thousand, yes, he paid two thousand. On a ten-thousand loan. I told him I'd come back next week.

c005-p_bernard/a0db94e9.speaker: c005-p_bernard
c005-p_bernard/a0db94e9.text: I collect from forty people a week. I don't remember every one.

c005-p_bernard/22c675dc.speaker: c005-p_bernard
c005-p_bernard/22c675dc.text: I lend money. I don't break heads. Dead men don't pay.

c005-p_tony/44a16251.speaker: c005-p_tony
c005-p_tony/44a16251.text: We argued about money. He said Saturday. Now there's no Saturday.

c005-p_fredrick/0fe79045.speaker: c005-p_fredrick
c005-p_fredrick/0fe79045.text: I know what people will say. Here.

c005-p_fredrick/a87d43a0.speaker: c005-p_fredrick
c005-p_fredrick/a87d43a0.text: I wanted his pitch. Through the county, with forms. Not like this.

c006-p_kelvin/c961cac3.speaker: c006-p_kelvin
c006-p_kelvin/c961cac3.text: I was only gone for lunch. Only lunch.

c006-p_kelvin/a575f9c9.speaker: c006-p_kelvin
c006-p_kelvin/a575f9c9.text: He shouted at me last week, said he'd dismiss me if I came late again. But he taught me everything. Everything.

c006-p_kelvin/8a2e6e26.speaker: c006-p_kelvin
c006-p_kelvin/8a2e6e26.text: Joel writes 'check inside' when something's wrong with a job. He never wrote it with two marks before.

c006-p_kelvin/2fe29008.speaker: c006-p_kelvin
c006-p_kelvin/2fe29008.text: Mr. Gakuru owns the shop. He and Joel argued about money for months. He went to Mombasa last night.

c006-p_kelvin/9822e226.speaker: c006-p_kelvin
c006-p_kelvin/9822e226.text: Mama Wambui on Accra Road. Githeri. She'll tell you.

c006-p_kelvin/a034a0dc.speaker: c006-p_kelvin
c006-p_kelvin/a034a0dc.text: I went for lunch at quarter to one at Mama Wambui's on Accra Road.

c006-p_aisha/07b45f76.speaker: c006-p_aisha
